author: Ainsley Platt
title: Arkansas cities receive millions in federal pollution cleanup funds - NewsBreak
text:
By Ainsley Platt ,
8 hours ago WASHINGTON, DC - The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) headquarters is seen on February 13, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Two Arkansas cities were awarded a combined $2.5 million in grants for pollution cleanup activities by the Environmental Protection Agency, the regulator announced Wednesday.
Russellville and Crossett will receive $1.5 million and $1 million, respectively, to conduct more than 70 environmental site assessments of brownfield sites. The funds will also be used to develop cleanup plans, and, in Crossett, to clean up the Crossett Municipal Building.
The grant awarded to Russellville covers the cities of Dover and Atkins as well. Priority sites for the grant include former dry cleaners and car sale businesses, vacant lots and historical storefronts.
A brownfield is not automatically a Superfund site, or a highly contaminated site that meets certain criteria set out in federal law and is managed under the EPA’s Superfund program. A property is considered a brownfield under federal law if it has a confirmed or suspected hazardous contaminant, such as heavy metals or asbestos, that affects how the land can be used or redeveloped.
The funding is part of more than $270 million in Brownfields Multipurpose, Assessment, and Cleanup grants announced by the EPA Wednesday.
The brownfields program began in 1995, and is related to the better known Superfund program, which addresses highly contaminated sites such as the Vertac chemical plant in Jacksonville.
The brownfields program was designed to help assess and clean up smaller properties like old gas stations that didn’t meet superfund criteria.
“Addressing environmental contamination and reusing brownfield properties revitalizes neighborhoods, drives local job creation, and unleashes new economic opportunities,” said Thomas Croci, the EPA’s acting assistant administrator for land and emergency management, in a press release.
